alice: Drafting onboarding runbook for a new cloud project + VNet in eu-central-1. Putting the checklist here, please review.

alice: ```
# Project + VNet onboarding runbook (draft)
1) Create cloud project/account with org tag: rw-inference-<team>-<region>
2) Enable APIs: compute, networking, iam, billing, quotas, kms
3) Create service accounts: infra-provisioner, node-agent, logging-ingest
4) Assign least-priv roles, ensure KMS access for infra-provisioner
5) VNet design: 10.40.0.0/16 for region (split into /20 per AZ)
   - Subnets per AZ: control plane (10.40.0.0/22), gpu-pool-az1 (10.40.8.0/22), gpu-pool-az2 (10.40.12.0/22), app-tier (10.40.16.0/20)
   - Private subnets only, NAT for outbound egress via managed NAT
6) Firewall: allow internal Pod<>Pod, allow control plane CIDRs, restrict mgmt ports to bastion + SRE IPs
7) Peering: peer to shared-services VNet (logging, metrics) with route tables + no-overlap check
8) Routing: prefer regional egress, add BGP routes only when needed
9) Quota checks: GPUs, vCPUs, IPs. Submit provider quota increase early (estimate: 32 A100s for initial pool)
10) Reservations: request capacity reservations for gpu family (A100/RTX) based on forecast
11) Cost tags: project, team, env, model-family, reserved-vs-burst
12) Monitoring hooks: Datadog + Prometheus exporter installed in bootstrap image
13) Validation steps (smoke): provisioning a 2-node GPU cluster, run perf-ml-infer smoke test, verify KV cache warmup, validate fallbacks
14) Handoff: create runbook in runbooks/region-eu-central-1, assign owner in oncall rota
15) Post-mortem triggers: any >5% request error or >200ms tail latency degradation after rollout
```

ben_infra: looks great. quick q: why /16? seems big for a single region

carlos_net: /16 gives us headroom for multiple environments + future AZ splits. we reserve /20 per AZ so we can carve without renumbering. also avoids clash with partner peering (we keep a 10.40/16 pool per region).

deepa_prodops: adding GPU ops notes: we should submit quota with expected initial commit and 90-day ramp. also add a checklist item to reserve capacity (provider-specific reservation id) and document fallback models (smaller quantized variants) to cut cost when capacity is tight.

alice: good call. adding explicit quota/reservation fields to runbook and where to store the reservation IDs (vault path: secret/projects/rw-inference/<proj>/reservations)

amanda_sre: Validation tests? add synthetic load for tail latency and a test for failover to fallback model. Also run an egress-path test: ensure logging traffic routes to shared-services via peering and that NAT gateway metrics are reported.

alice: updated validation section. short checklist added below in thread for oncall handoff:

alice: ```
Handoff checklist for oncall owner:
- Confirm project + billing link exists and tags set
- Verify service accounts and KMS permissions
- Confirm VNet and subnets created and route tables attached
- Confirm peering established and test ping between logging/metrics endpoints
- Deploy 2-node GPU cluster via infra-provisioner svc acct
- Run smoke perf test (perf-ml-infer --model=resnet-small --requests=100)
- Confirm Datadog dashboards show node & pod metrics and GPU utilization
- Upload reservation ID and quota ticket link to runbook page
- Set SLO alert: tail latency > 200ms -> paging policy
- Mark owner in runbooks page and add calendar block for first-week monitoring
```
